hints.title: Significant Place Value Greedy Obstacle
hints.text: A larger digit at a more significant place value always makes the number strictly larger than a smaller digit would. How can iterating from left to right and discarding preceding peaks build the minimum number greedily?

hints.title: Monotonic Non-Decreasing Peak Invariant
hints.text: If digit d_i > d_{i+1}, removing d_i immediately yields a strictly smaller prefix. Maintaining digits in non-decreasing order while k > 0 minimizes the overall value.

hints.title: Peak Eviction and Trimming Procedure
hints.text: Traverse digits. While k > 0, the digit list is non-empty, and its last digit > current digit, pop the last digit and decrement k. Append current digit. If k remains > 0, slice off the trailing k digits. Strip leading zeros and return '0' if empty.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: N: length of num string (1 <= N <= 10^5)
k: number of digits to remove (1 <= k <= N)
complexity.notes: Each digit is pushed and popped at most once; linear time digit trimming.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Enumerating all combinations of choosing N - k digits out of N takes exponential binomial time.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Using an auxiliary character list enables O(1) removals of peak digits from the tail.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Handling edge cases such as leading zeros, remaining k > 0 for monotonic inputs, and k == N.
